set.title: Profile fold apply loop
set.body: Cold fold at the 30k-event reference is ~109 ms and apply-bound (~85 ms replaying events, ~2.8 us/event; body size adds only ~8 ms). Profile the apply loop before optimizing: find whether ts parsing or per-field dict churn dominates. Measure, then decide.

set.title: Implement size-triggered body spill
set.body: Per spec section 13.2: bodies stay inline; a body exceeding a configurable threshold (default 4096 bytes) spills to bodies/<id>.md on write, and rp show resolves either form transparently. Section 5.3 already permits both shapes, so no schema change. Include a doctor check that every referenced sidecar file exists. Threshold tuning should use the by-type body percentiles from the rp stats ticket once a real corpus exists.

set.title: Set-wise three-way merge for labels
set.body: Known phase-1 gap. Labels (and other set fields) currently merge by per-field last-write-wins, which silently loses concurrent set additions from two runners. Implement set-wise three-way merge so concurrent labels+ ops compose.

set.title: rp stats command
set.body: Extend rp stats to report body-size percentiles split by ticket type (epic vs task), so the bimodal body distribution behind the section 13.2 spill decision can be observed. This supplies signals D1/D2 once a real corpus exists and tunes the 4096-byte spill threshold.

set.title: Compaction loses events if interrupted between log rewrite and archive append
set.body: src/rohrpost/compact.py run() rewrites (truncates) log.jsonl to only the kept events (_rewrite_log at :177) BEFORE appending the archived events to the archive buckets (the _append_archive loop at :178-179). A crash or SIGKILL between those two steps permanently loses the to-be-archived events: in that window they are removed from the log but not yet present in any archive file, existing only in the in-memory archive_buckets dict. Spec §6.1 specifies the crash-safe order - archive first (step 2), then rewrite the log (step 3) - which leaves only dedupable duplicates on a crash (the fold drops them by event id). Fix: append to archive files first, then rewrite the log, all still under store.file_lock. Add a regression test that simulates an interruption between the steps and asserts no events are lost.

set.title: Doctor authentication probes for all providers
set.body: rp doctor (spec §10.1) must verify remote credentials actually authenticate, not merely that a token env var is present. GitHub already has a real probe (providers/github.py + the github branch of doctor.py _remote_authenticated). The generic fallback (doctor.py _remote_authenticated, ~:206-215) only checks token presence and returns True for a present-but-invalid or expired token, so a configured non-github remote with a dead token passes the check. Each provider needs its own authentication probe in rp doctor. Tracked per provider below.

set.title: Doctor authentication probe: GitLab
set.body: Add a real authentication probe for the GitLab remote to rp doctor, so a present-but-invalid or expired token is reported as failing rather than passing. Today the generic _remote_authenticated (doctor.py, ~:206-215) only checks token presence for non-github remotes (spec audit finding #4), returning True for a dead token. Depends on the GitLab provider landing (phase 3).

set.title: Body-merge conflicts must keep conflict markers in the body
set.body: Spec §8.3 requires that on a body-merge collision the conflict markers (<<<<<<< / ======= / >>>>>>>) are kept IN the body and the ticket is flagged. The code computes the marker-laden three-way merge in _merge_body (merge.py ~:120-130) but then DISCARDS it, recording only the original local/remote values in a FieldConflict; _flag_conflict (sync.py ~:234-267) writes status=review + a conflict:<remote> label + a comment, but never updates the body - so the markers a human or agent needs in order to resolve the conflict are lost. The merge.py module docstring (~:17-18) already claims "keeping conflict markers on collision", which the flag path does not do. Fix: under the default flag policy, write the marker-laden merged text to the body in addition to the existing label/comment. Add coverage asserting the markers survive in the body (current tests/test_merge.py:59-64 only checks the flag, not the markers).
